correctness.rationale: Equations (1)-(3) follow from the explicit inverse covariance and two Gaussian marginal cutoff identities. With two positive canonical correlations, mixed partials force affine fields, marginal weighted divergence forces skew linear rotations, and the anisotropic precision terms eliminate them except on the repeated-singular-value stratum. With rank-one cross-covariance, scalar Gaussian ODEs and L2 force every field component to zero. At zero correlation, radial rotations provide infinitely many exact null fields. The fixed diffusion 2Sigma admits a stable OU realization in all regimes. The packaged exact rational checker verifies 12 low-degree nullities plus 2 direct rotation substitutions but is not relied on as infinite-dimensional proof.

value.rationale: The two-cycle exception to inverse stationary drift identification is central to the motivating 2026 nonlinear theorem. This result completely resolves a natural four-node two-feedback-block Gaussian regime: one cross-canonical correlation eliminates even nonlinear ambiguities, repeated positive correlations create precisely one circulation, and complete independence yields an infinite-dimensional ambiguity. The sharp full phase diagram identifies a structural geometry, not a tiny numerical optimization or arbitrary parameter slice; it has direct interpretability for sparse diffusion inverse problems.
